canonical_topic: Why Asian options have lower implied volatility
definition: Averaging a series of random prices produces a result with less dispersion (lower volatility) than any single price drawn from that same series.
core_idea: Because the settlement is an average rather than a single spot observation, the effective volatility priced into an Asian option is lower than that of an equivalent European option, making it cheaper for buyers and safer for sellers.
key_points: The statistical reduction in dispersion from averaging is the mechanical reason Asian options price with lower implied volatility.
Lower volatility pricing translates to lower premiums than a comparable European option.
This also makes the position less risky from the seller's perspective.
relationships: Follows from Asian option payoff definition
Affects premium relative to European options
trading_implications: Buyers pay less for Asian options than for comparable standard options because of the reduced effective volatility.
Sellers of Asian options take on less risk than sellers of comparable European options.
caveats: One might assume an average-price option should price the same as a European option with the same underlying and strike; the averaging mechanically lowers effective volatility, so it does not.
